div class=3D"markdown-heading" dir=3D"auto"><h1 tabindex=3D"-1" class=3D"he=
ading-element" dir=3D"auto">ML-In-The-Loop Workflow for Molecular Design wi=
th Parsl</h1><a id=3D"user-content-ml-in-the-loop-workflow-for-molecular-de=
sign-with-parsl" class=3D"anchor" aria-label=3D"Permalink: ML-In-The-Loop W=
orkflow for Molecular Design with Parsl" href=3D"https://github.com/argonne=
-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Coupling-Sim-AI/ml-in-the-loop=
/README.md#ml-in-the-loop-workflow-for-molecular-design-with-parsl"><svg cl=
ass=3D"octicon octicon-link" viewBox=3D"0 0 16 16" version=3D"1.1" width=3D=
"16" height=3D"16" aria-hidden=3D"true"><path d=3D"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3=
.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.=
042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0=
 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.04=
2Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.7=
51.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 =
0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 =
0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir=3D"auto">This example demonstrates a simple molecular design applica=
tion combining simulations with machine learning (ML) training and inferenc=
e. The objective is to efficiently identify molecules with the largest ioni=
zation energies from a large dataset of potential candidates.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">The example was adapted from an <a href=3D"https://github.c=
om/ExaWorks/molecular-design-parsl-demo/tree/main">ExaWorks demo</a> develo=
ped by Logan Ward, ANL.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">The ionization energy (IE) of a molecule is the amount of e=
nergy required to remove one electron from the molecule in its ground state=
 to produce a positively charged ion.
IE can be computed using various simulation packages (here we use <a href=
=3D"https://xtb-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contents.html" rel=3D"nofollo=
w">xTB</a>); however, execution of these simulations can be expensive, and =
thus, given a finite compute budget and a large set of molecules to screen,=
 we must carefully select which molecules to explore by simulation.
To help reduce the cost of screening large datasets of potential candidate =
molecules, we use machine learning, specifically a k-nearest neighbors (KNN=
) regressor, to predict the IE of molecules based on previously simulated d=
ata.
We then employ an iterative process often called <a href=3D"https://pubs.ac=
s.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.chemmater.0c00768" rel=3D"nofollow">active learni=
ng</a> to simulate the best identified compounds and retrain the KNN model =
to improve the accuracy of predictions.
A schematic of the active learning, or ML-in-the-loop, workflow is shown be=
low.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto"><a target=3D"_blank" rel=3D"noopener noreferrer" href=3D"ht=
tps://github.com/argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Coupli=
ng-Sim-AI/figures/workflow.svg"><img src=3D"https://github.com/argonne-lcf/=
ai-science-training-series/raw/main/03-Coupling-Sim-AI/figures/workflow.svg=
" alt=3D"workflow" style=3D"max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir=3D"auto">For this example, we use <a href=3D"https://github.com/Pars=
l/parsl">Parsl</a> to execute functions (simulation, model training, and in=
ference) in parallel. Parsl allows us to establish dependencies in the work=
flow and to execute the workflow on arbitrary computing infrastructure, fro=
m laptops to supercomputers. We show how Parsl's integration with Python's =
native concurrency library (i.e., <a href=3D"https://docs.python.org/3/libr=
ary/concurrent.futures.html#module-concurrent.futures" rel=3D"nofollow"><co=
de>concurrent.futures</code></a>) lets you write applications that dynamica=
lly respond to the completion of asynchronous tasks.</p>
<div class=3D"markdown-heading" dir=3D"auto"><h3 tabindex=3D"-1" class=3D"h=
eading-element" dir=3D"auto">Parsl Setup</h3><a id=3D"user-content-parsl-se=
tup" class=3D"anchor" aria-label=3D"Permalink: Parsl Setup" href=3D"https:/=
/github.com/argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Coupling-Si=
m-AI/ml-in-the-loop/README.md#parsl-setup"><svg class=3D"octicon octicon-li=
nk" viewBox=3D"0 0 16 16" version=3D"1.1" width=3D"16" height=3D"16" aria-h=
idden=3D"true"><path d=3D"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2=
.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.=
018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25=
a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998=
 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-=
1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0=
 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.9=
98 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir=3D"auto">We first configure Parsl to make use of available resources=
. In this case, we configure Parsl to run on the Polaris supercomputer. Thi=
s example does not use GPUs (both the xTB simulations and the KNN model can=
 run efficiently on CPUs), so we set one worker per physical CPU for a tota=
l of 32 workers per node.  For a GPU application, we would change the confi=
guration to pin one worker per GPU as in the <a href=3D"https://github.com/=
argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Coupling-Sim-AI/produce=
r-consumer/parsl_config.py">producer-consumer example</a>.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">One of the benefits of Parsl is that we can change this con=
figuration to make use of different resources without modifying the applica=
tion code. For example, we can configure Parsl to use more cores on the loc=
al machine or to use many nodes on a Supercomputer or Cloud. The <a href=3D=
"https://parsl.readthedocs.io/en/stable/userguide/configuring.html" rel=3D"=
nofollow">Parsl website</a> describes how Parsl can be configured for diffe=
rent resources.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">The Parsl Config for this example is in the file <a href=3D=
"https://github.com/argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Cou=
pling-Sim-AI/ml-in-the-loop/parsl_config.py">parsl_config.py</a>.</p>
<div class=3D"markdown-heading" dir=3D"auto"><h3 tabindex=3D"-1" class=3D"h=
eading-element" dir=3D"auto">Creating a Parsl Python App and Launching a Si=
mulation</h3><a id=3D"user-content-creating-a-parsl-python-app-and-launchin=
g-a-simulation" class=3D"anchor" aria-label=3D"Permalink: Creating a Parsl =
Python App and Launching a Simulation" href=3D"https://github.com/argonne-l=
cf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Coupling-Sim-AI/ml-in-the-loop/R=
EADME.md#creating-a-parsl-python-app-and-launching-a-simulation"><svg class=
=3D"octicon octicon-link" viewBox=3D"0 0 16 16" version=3D"1.1" width=3D"16=
" height=3D"16" aria-hidden=3D"true"><path d=3D"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 =
3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042=
.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 =
0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm=
-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.=
751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0=
 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0=
 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir=3D"auto">Second, we look at a minimal example to understand how to s=
ubmit a Python function with Parsl, as shown in <a href=3D"https://github.c=
om/argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Coupling-Sim-AI/ml-i=
n-the-loop/1_run_simulation.py">1_run_simulation.py</a>.
Using the <code>compute_vertical</code> function, which computes the ioniza=
tion energy of a molecule with the xTB package, we prepare this function to=
 run with Parsl by wrapping it with Parsl's <code>python_app</code>:</p>
<div class=3D"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relati=
ve overflow-auto" dir=3D"auto"><pre><span class=3D"pl-s1">compute_vertical_=
app</span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span> <span class=3D"pl-en">python_ap=
p</span>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">compute_vertical</span>)</pre><div class=3D"=
zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label=3D"Copy" class=3D"ClipboardButton btn btn-in=
visible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-cen=
ter" data-copy-feedback=3D"Copied!" data-tooltip-direction=3D"w" value=3D"c=
ompute_vertical_app =3D python_app(compute_vertical)" tabindex=3D"0" role=
=3D"button">
      <svg aria-hidden=3D"true" height=3D"16" viewBox=3D"0 0 16 16" version=
=3D"1.1" width=3D"16" data-view-component=3D"true" class=3D"octicon octicon=

    <path d=3D"M0 6.75C0 5.784.784 5 1.75 5h1.5a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5h-1.5a.25=

 0 0-.25-.25Z"></path>
</svg>
      <svg aria-hidden=3D"true" height=3D"16" viewBox=3D"0 0 16 16" version=

 0L2.22 9.28a.751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018L6 10.94l6.7=
2-6.72a.75.75 0 0 1 1.06 0Z"></path>

    </clipboard-copy>

<p dir=3D"auto">This new object is a Parsl <code>PythonApp</code>. It can b=
e invoked like the original function, but instead of immediately executing,=
 the function may be run asynchronously by Parsl. Instead of the result, th=
e call will immediately return a <code>Future</code>, which we can use to r=
etrieve the result or obtain the status of the running task.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">For example, invoking the <code>compute_vertical_app</code>=
 with the SMILES for water, <code>O</code>, returns a Future and schedules =
<code>compute_vertical</code> for execution in the background.</p>
<div class=3D"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relati=
ve overflow-auto" dir=3D"auto"><pre><span class=3D"pl-s1">future</span> <sp=
an class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span> <span class=3D"pl-en">compute_vertical_app</s=
pan>(<span class=3D"pl-s">'O'</span>) <span class=3D"pl-c">#  Run water as =
a demonstration (O is the SMILES for water)</span></pre><div class=3D"zeroc=
lipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label=3D"Copy" class=3D"ClipboardButton btn btn-in=
visible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-cen=
ter" data-copy-feedback=3D"Copied!" data-tooltip-direction=3D"w" value=3D"f=
uture =3D compute_vertical_app('O') #  Run water as a demonstration (O is t=
he SMILES for water)" tabindex=3D"0" role=3D"button">
      <svg aria-hidden=3D"true" height=3D"16" viewBox=3D"0 0 16 16" version=
=3D"1.1" width=3D"16" data-view-component=3D"true" class=3D"octicon octicon=
-copy js-clipboard-copy-icon">
    <path d=3D"M0 6.75C0 5.784.784 5 1.75 5h1.5a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5h-1.5a.25=

75 0 0 1 1.5 0v1.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 9.25 16h-7.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 0 14.25Z"><=
/path><path d=3D"M5 1.75C5 .784 5.784 0 6.75 0h7.5C15.216 0 16 .784 16 1.75=
v7.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.25 11h-7.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 5 9.25Zm1.75-.25a.25.25 =
0 0 0-.25.25v7.5c0 .138.112.25.25.25h7.5a.25.25 0 0 0 .25-.25v-7.5a.25.25 0=
 0 0-.25-.25Z"></path>
</svg>
      <svg aria-hidden=3D"true" height=3D"16" viewBox=3D"0 0 16 16" version=
=3D"1.1" width=3D"16" data-view-component=3D"true" class=3D"octicon octicon=

    <path d=3D"M13.78 4.22a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.06l-7.25 7.25a.75.75 0 0 1-1.06=
 0L2.22 9.28a.751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018L6 10.94l6.7=
2-6.72a.75.75 0 0 1 1.06 0Z"></path>
</svg>
    </clipboard-copy>
  </div></div>
<p dir=3D"auto">We can access the result of this computation by asking the =
future for the <code>result()</code>. If the computation isn't finished yet=
, then the call to <code>.result()</code> will block until the result is re=
ady.</p>
<div class=3D"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relati=
ve overflow-auto" dir=3D"auto"><pre><span class=3D"pl-s1">ie</span> <span c=
lass=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span> <span class=3D"pl-s1">future</span>.<span class=

eading-element" dir=3D"auto">Launching Multiple Tasks in Parallel with Data=

<p dir=3D"auto">Now we can look at a slightly more complex workflow which e=
xecutes multiple tasks in parallel with data dependencies, as shown in <a h=
ref=3D"https://github.com/argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/=
03-Coupling-Sim-AI/ml-in-the-loop/2_training_and_inference.py">2_training_a=
nd_inference.py</a>.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">We use a standard Python loop to submit a set of simulation=
s for parallel execution. As above, each invocation returns a <code>Future<=
/code> immediately, so this code should finish within a few milliseconds.</=
p>
<div class=3D"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relati=
ve overflow-auto" dir=3D"auto"><pre><span class=3D"pl-s1">smiles</span> <sp=
an class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span> <span class=3D"pl-s1">search_space</span>.<sp=
an class=3D"pl-c1">sample</span>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">initial_count</span>=
)[<span class=3D"pl-s">'smiles'</span>]
<span class=3D"pl-s1">futures</span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span> [<spa=
n class=3D"pl-en">compute_vertical_app</span>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">s</span=
>) <span class=3D"pl-k">for</span> <span class=3D"pl-s1">s</span> <span cla=
ss=3D"pl-c1">in</span> <span class=3D"pl-s1">smiles</span>]</pre><div class=
=3D"zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label=3D"Copy" class=3D"ClipboardButton btn btn-in=
visible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-cen=
ter" data-copy-feedback=3D"Copied!" data-tooltip-direction=3D"w" value=3D"s=
miles =3D search_space.sample(initial_count)['smiles']
futures =3D [compute_vertical_app(s) for s in smiles]" tabindex=3D"0" role=
=3D"button">

<p dir=3D"auto">Because we do not call <code>.result()</code> immediately, =
this code does not wait for any results to be ready. Instead, Parsl is runn=
ing the computations concurrently in the background. Parsl manages sending =
work to each worker process, collecting results, and feeding new work to wo=
rkers as new tasks are submitted.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">The futures produced by Parsl are based on Python's <a href=
=3D"https://docs.python.org/3/library/concurrent.futures.html#future-object=
s" rel=3D"nofollow">native "Future"</a> object,
so we can use Python's utility functions to work with them.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">In collecting simulation results, we use <code>as_completed=
</code> to take an iterable (in this case, a list) of futures and to yield =
as each future completes.  Thus, we progress and handle each simulation as =
it completes.  The data are loaded into a pandas <code>DataFrame</code> con=
taining the randomly sampled molecules alongside the simulated ionization e=
nergy (<code>ie</code>). In addition, the code above has stored some metada=
ta (<code>batch</code> and <code>time</code>), which we will use later.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">The next part of the script creates a machine learning mode=
l to estimate the outcome of new computations (i.e., ionization energy) and=
 uses it to rapidly scan the search space.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">We are going to use RDKit and scikit-learn to train a k-nea=
rest neighbor model that uses Morgan fingerprints to define similarity (see=
 <a href=3D"https://github.com/WardLT/applied-ai-for-materials/blob/main/mo=
lecular-property-prediction/chemoinformatics/2_ml-with-fingerprints.ipynb">=
notes from a UChicago AI course</a> for more detail). In short, the functio=
n trains a model that first populates a list of certain substructures (Morg=
an fingerprints, specifically) and then trains a model that predicts the IE=
 of a new molecule by averaging those with the most similar substructures.<=
/p>
<p dir=3D"auto">The training and inferencing scripts are provided in the <c=
ode>chemfunctions</code> module.
We define the Parsl apps for these functions as before with the <code>pytho=
n_app</code> API</p>
<div class=3D"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relati=
ve overflow-auto" dir=3D"auto"><pre><span class=3D"pl-s1">train_model_app</=
span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span> <span class=3D"pl-en">python_app</sp=
an>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">train_model</span>)
<span class=3D"pl-s1">inference_app</span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span>=
 <span class=3D"pl-en">python_app</span>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">run_model</s=
pan>)</pre><div class=3D"zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label=3D"Copy" class=3D"ClipboardButton btn btn-in=
visible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-cen=
ter" data-copy-feedback=3D"Copied!" data-tooltip-direction=3D"w" value=3D"t=
rain_model_app =3D python_app(train_model)
inference_app =3D python_app(run_model)" tabindex=3D"0" role=3D"button">

<p dir=3D"auto">One of the unique features of Parsl is that it can create w=
orkflows on-the-fly directly from Python. Parsl workflows are chains of fun=
ctions, connected by dynamic dependencies (i.e., data passed between Parsl =
<code>apps</code>), that can run in parallel when possible.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">To establish the workflow, we pass the future created by ex=
ecuting one function as an input to another Parsl function.  We therefore p=
ass a future for the <code>train_model_app</code> to the <code>inference_ap=
p</code>, and we only have to wait for the completion of the inference futu=
re.  Parsl will automatically wait for the training future before running i=
nference:</p>
<div class=3D"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relati=
ve overflow-auto" dir=3D"auto"><pre><span class=3D"pl-s1">train_future</spa=
n> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span> <span class=3D"pl-en">train_model_app</=
span>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">train_data</span>)
<span class=3D"pl-s1">inference_future</span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</sp=
an> <span class=3D"pl-en">inference_app</span>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">train_=
future</span>, <span class=3D"pl-s1">chunk</span>)
<span class=3D"pl-s1">inference_future</span>.<span class=3D"pl-c1">result<=
/span>()</pre><div class=3D"zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label=3D"Copy" class=3D"ClipboardButton btn btn-in=
visible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-cen=
ter" data-copy-feedback=3D"Copied!" data-tooltip-direction=3D"w" value=3D"t=
rain_future =3D train_model_app(train_data)
inference_future =3D inference_app(train_future, chunk)
inference_future.result()" tabindex=3D"0" role=3D"button">

<p dir=3D"auto">While this script runs inferences in parallel, we can defin=
e the final part of the workflow to combine results into a single DataFrame=
 using <code>combine_inferences</code>.</p>
<div class=3D"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relati=
ve overflow-auto" dir=3D"auto"><pre><span class=3D"pl-en">@<span class=3D"p=
l-s1">python_app</span></span>
<span class=3D"pl-k">def</span> <span class=3D"pl-en">combine_inferences</s=
pan>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">inputs</span><span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span>[])=
:
    <span class=3D"pl-s">"""Concatenate a series of inferences into a singl=
e DataFrame</span>
<span class=3D"pl-s">    Args:</span>
<span class=3D"pl-s">        inputs: a list of the component DataFrames</sp=
an>
<span class=3D"pl-s">    Returns:</span>
<span class=3D"pl-s">        A single DataFrame containing the same inferen=
ces</span>
<span class=3D"pl-s">    """</span>
    <span class=3D"pl-k">import</span> <span class=3D"pl-s1">pandas</span> =
<span class=3D"pl-k">as</span> <span class=3D"pl-s1">pd</span>
    <span class=3D"pl-k">return</span> <span class=3D"pl-s1">pd</span>.<spa=
n class=3D"pl-c1">concat</span>(<span class=3D"pl-s1">inputs</span>, <span =
class=3D"pl-s1">ignore_index</span><span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span><span cl=
ass=3D"pl-c1">True</span>)</pre><div class=3D"zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label=3D"Copy" class=3D"ClipboardButton btn btn-in=
visible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-cen=
ter" data-copy-feedback=3D"Copied!" data-tooltip-direction=3D"w" value=3D"@=
python_app
def combine_inferences(inputs=3D[]):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Concatenate a series of inferences into a single Data=
Frame
    Args:
        inputs: a list of the component DataFrames
    Returns:
        A single DataFrame containing the same inferences
    &quot;&quot;&quot;
    import pandas as pd
    return pd.concat(inputs, ignore_index=3DTrue)" tabindex=3D"0" role=3D"b=
utton">

<p dir=3D"auto">In defining <code>combine_inferences</code>, <code>python_a=
pp</code> is used as a decorator directly on the function definition (earli=
er we defined a regular function, and then applied <code>python_app</code> =
afterwards).
We pass the <code>inference_futures</code> as inputs to <code>combine_infer=
ences</code> such that Parsl knows to establish a dependency between these =
two functions. Since Parsl will ensure that <code>train_future</code> must =
complete before any of the <code>inference_app</code> tasks start, and all =
of the <code>inference_app</code> tasks must be finished before <code>combi=
ne_inferences</code> starts, all we need to do is wait on the result of the=
 <code>combine_inferences</code> future to ensure the workflow completes an=
d dependencies are honored.</p>

<p dir=3D"auto">Finally, we build the full active learning workflow (see <a=
 href=3D"https://github.com/argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/mai=
n/03-Coupling-Sim-AI/ml-in-the-loop/3_ml_in_the_loop.py">3_ml_in_the_loop.p=
y</a>), which uses the ML model to pick a batch of simulations, runs the si=
mulations in parallel, and then uses the data to retrain the model before r=
epeating the loop.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">Our application uses <code>train_model_app</code>, <code>in=
ference_app</code>, and <code>combine_inferences</code> as above, but after=
 running an iteration, it picks the predicted best molecules and runs the <=
code>compute_vertical_app</code> to run the xTB simulation on those top can=
didates.  The workflow then repeatedly retrains the model using these resul=
ts until a pre-determined number of simulations have been trained.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">The workflow is initialized with the following parameters, =
which determine how much data is to be generated via simulation for pre-tra=
ining of the KNN model, the maximum size of the training dataset (thus also=
 the maximum number of simulations to perform), and how many new simulation=
s to perform and training data points to generate for each active learning =
iteration. These parameters strike a balance between pre-training and fine-=
tuning the model and can influence the accuracy of the model.</p>
<div class=3D"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relati=
ve overflow-auto" dir=3D"auto"><pre><span class=3D"pl-c"># Define parameter=
s for the workflow</span>
<span class=3D"pl-s1">initial_training_count</span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=
=3D</span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">8</span>  <span class=3D"pl-c"># Number of=
 training samples to collect for first model training</span>
<span class=3D"pl-s1">max_training_count</span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</=
span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">24</span>  <span class=3D"pl-c"># Maximum numbe=
r of training samples to collect for training</span>
<span class=3D"pl-s1">batch_size</span> <span class=3D"pl-c1">=3D</span> <s=
pan class=3D"pl-c1">4</span>  <span class=3D"pl-c"># Number of molecules to=
 simulate in each iteration of active learning loop</span></pre><div class=
=3D"zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label=3D"Copy" class=3D"ClipboardButton btn btn-in=
visible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-cen=

 Define parameters for the workflow
initial_training_count =3D 8  # Number of training samples to collect for f=
irst model training
max_training_count =3D 24  # Maximum number of training samples to collect =
for training
batch_size =3D 4  # Number of molecules to simulate in each iteration of ac=
tive learning loop" tabindex=3D"0" role=3D"button">

<p dir=3D"auto">Tune the parameters of the ML-in-the-loop active learning w=
orkflow in order to find molecules with the largest ionization energy in th=
e shortest possible time.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">Use the PBS submit script <a href=3D"https://github.com/arg=
onne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Coupling-Sim-AI/ml-in-the-=
loop/4_submit_multinode.sh">4_submit_multinode.sh</a> to run the full workf=
low on 1 or multiple nodes of Polaris.
Note that all that should be needed for this exercise is to change the valu=
es of the <code>initial_training_count</code>, <code>max_training_count</co=
de> and <code>batch_size</code> variables at the top of the <code>3_ml_in_t=
he_loop.py</code> script in order to balance pre-training with fine-tuning =
of the model.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto">The script will generate a figure with the results of the a=
ctive learning loop called <code>parsl_ml_in_the_loop.png</code>. Use this =
figure to determine the performance of your tests. Once ready to submit, si=
mply commit the repository with the updated image showing your best results=
, which will automatically be populated below in this README file.</p>
<p dir=3D"auto"><a target=3D"_blank" rel=3D"noopener noreferrer" href=3D"ht=
tps://github.com/argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/blob/main/03-Coupli=
ng-Sim-AI/ml-in-the-loop/parsl_ml_in_the_loop.png"><img src=3D"https://gith=
ub.com/argonne-lcf/ai-science-training-series/raw/main/03-Coupling-Sim-AI/m=
l-in-the-loop/parsl_ml_in_the_loop.png" alt=3D"results" style=3D"max-width:=
 100%;"></a></p>
</article></div></section></div></div></div>   </div></div></div></div></di=
v></div></div><div id=3D"find-result-marks-container" class=3D"Box-sc-62in7=

</react-app>

</turbo-frame>

.suggest-icon svg::after, .suggest-icon path::after { top: -5px; right: -5p=
x; width: 5px; height: 5px; background-color: rgb(108, 132, 233); }

: 6px; background-color: rgb(108, 132, 233); border-radius: 50%; }

.suggest-icon .suggest-icon-bubble:nth-of-type(2n) { width: 4px; height: 4p=
x; background-color: rgb(158, 123, 255); }

x; }

-base-size-4); }

 }
